function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

function.name: write_markdown_tool

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

function.name: write_html_tool

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide to the most common “tools” you can use to search for, compare, and book flights.  I’ve grouped them into three broad categories:

| Category | Tool / Service | What it offers | Typical use‑case |
|----------|----------------|----------------|------------------|
| **Flight‑search APIs** | **Amadeus for Developers** | Full flight search, booking, and ancillary services (seat selection, baggage, etc.).  Supports multi‑city, round‑trip, one‑way, and even “smart” pricing. | Integrate flight booking into your own app or website. |
| | **Skyscanner API** | Search for flights, hotels, car rentals.  Provides price alerts and “best‑price” data. | Build a price‑comparison widget or a travel‑planning tool. |
| | **Travelport Universal API** | Enterprise‑grade booking engine with global inventory. | Large travel agencies or corporate travel portals. |
| | **Sabre APIs** | Flight search, booking, and ancillary services.  Offers “Sabre API Hub” for multiple travel services. | Travel agencies, OTAs, and corporate travel solutions. |
| | **Google Flights API** (unofficial) | Not a public API, but you can scrape or use the Google Flights web interface via automation. | Quick prototyping or research. |
| | **Kayak API** (via Kayak for Developers) | Flight search, price alerts, and booking. | Travel comparison sites. |
| | **Expedia Rapid API** | Flight search, booking, and hotel/car rental integration. | Travel agencies, corporate travel. |
| | **Priceline API** | Flight search and booking. | Travel agencies, corporate travel. |
| | **CheapOair API** | Flight search and booking. | Travel agencies, corporate travel. |
| | **FlightAware API** | Real‑time flight status, not booking, but useful for itinerary tracking. | Travel apps that need live flight data. |
| | **OpenSky API** | Real‑time flight data (positions, status). | Aviation analytics, flight tracking apps. |
| | **FlightStats API** | Flight status, delays, and historical data. | Travel apps that need reliability metrics. |
| | **IATA API** | Global flight data, codes, and schedules. | Data‑driven travel analytics. |
| | **FlightRadar24 API** (via third‑party) | Live flight tracking. | Flight tracking widgets. |
| | **Airline‑specific APIs** (e.g., Delta, United, Lufthansa) | Direct booking and ancillary services. | Airline‑direct booking portals. |
| **Flight‑search & booking websites / apps** | **Google Flights** | Fast search, price graph, “Explore” feature. | Quick price comparison. |
| | **Skyscanner** | Multi‑carrier search, price alerts, “Everywhere” search. | Budget travelers, price‑alert setups. |
| | **Kayak** | Price comparison, price alerts, “Price Forecast.” | Price‑forecasting and comparison. |
| | **Expedia** | Flights + hotels + car rentals. | All‑in‑one travel booking. |
| | **Priceline** | Flights + hotels + car rentals. | “Name Your Own Price” deals. |
| | **Orbitz** | Flights + hotels + car rentals. | US‑centric travel booking. |
| | **Hotwire** | “Hot Rate” deals for flights. | Last‑minute deals. |
| | **CheapOair** | Flights + hotels + car rentals. | Budget travel. |
| | **Momondo** | Price comparison across many OTAs. | Price‑comparison. |
| | **Travelocity** | Flights + hotels + car rentals. | US‑centric travel booking. |
| | **Trip.com** | Flights + hotels + car rentals. | Asian market focus. |
| | **Airbnb Experiences** (for flight‑related experiences) | Not a flight booking tool, but can be used for travel planning. | Travel planning. |
| | **Airline websites** (Delta, United, Southwest, etc.) | Direct booking, loyalty points, seat selection. | Loyalty‑program users. |
| | **Mobile apps** (Google Flights, Skyscanner, Kayak, Hopper) | Price prediction, alerts, booking. | On‑the‑go travelers. |
| **Travel agencies & corporate portals** | **Concur Travel** | Corporate travel booking, expense integration. | Corporate travel. |
| | **Egencia** | Corporate travel, expense management. | Corporate travel. |
| | **TravelPerk** | Corporate travel, expense integration. | Corporate travel. |
| | **CWT** | Corporate travel, expense integration. | Corporate travel. |
| | **American Express Travel** | Corporate & personal travel booking. | Corporate travel. |
| | **Booking.com** | Flights + hotels + car rentals. | All‑in‑one travel booking. |
| | **Agoda** | Flights + hotels + car rentals. | Asian market focus. |
| | **TripAdvisor Flights** | Flight search + reviews. | Price comparison + reviews. |
| | **Travel agencies (e.g., Thomas Cook, TUI)** | Full travel packages. | Package holidays. |

---

### How to choose the right tool

| Need | Recommended tool(s) |
|------|---------------------|
| **Build a custom booking widget** | Amadeus, Skyscanner, Sabre, Travelport |
| **Quick price comparison** | Skyscanner, Kayak, Momondo |
| **Corporate travel portal** | Concur, Egencia, TravelPerk, CWT |
| **Real‑time flight status** | FlightAware, FlightStats, OpenSky |
| **Price alerts & predictions** | Hopper, Skyscanner, Kayak |
| **All‑in‑one travel booking** | Expedia, Priceline, Orbitz, Booking.com |
| **Airline‑direct booking** | Airline APIs (Delta, United, etc.) |
| **Data‑driven analytics** | IATA, FlightStats, OpenSky, FlightRadar24 |

---

### Quick start for developers

If you’re looking to integrate flight booking into your own app or website, here’s a minimal workflow using the **Amadeus for Developers** API:

1. **Sign up** at https://developers.amadeus.com/ and create an app to get your `client_id` and `client_secret`.
2. **Obtain an access token** (OAuth 2.0) via the `/v1/security/oauth2/token` endpoint.
3. **Search for flights** using the `/v2/shopping/flight-offers` endpoint.  
   Example request:
   ```bash
   curl -X GET "https://test.api.amadeus.com/v2/shopping/flight-offers?originLocationCode=NYC&destinationLocationCode=LON&departureDate=2026-12-01&adults=1" \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
   ```
4. **Book a flight** using the `/v2/shopping/flight-offers/booking` endpoint, passing the selected offer ID and passenger details.
5. **Handle payment** via Amadeus’ payment integration or your own payment gateway.

---

### Final note

The flight‑booking ecosystem is constantly evolving.  Some APIs (e.g., Google Flights) are not publicly documented, so you’ll often rely on third‑party wrappers or web scraping.  Always check the terms of service and rate limits before integrating. Happy booking!
